clue.text: Slowly cooks fruit in vessel

parts.note: steams describes cooking gently in vapour
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A recipe note about stewing fruit slowly in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a cooking pot in the surface, but it is the definition: a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power is a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: A good loser is object of mockery

definitions.meaning: someone who takes defeat cheerfully and fairly, a decent type
a butt of jokes, a plaything for others' amusement

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a fair-minded loser, and a laughing stock or plaything.

clue.text: Watch bishop going over argument, surprised it's raised

indicators.note: in a down clue the bishop sits above, going over, the next piece

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A spectator sees a clergyman tackle a dispute and is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: when you are surprised, this facial feature is what goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift the hairy ridge above each eye in astonishment, a cryptic description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: People at fault, gravely so

parts.note: mortals are human beings
in can mean at, as in 'in the office' or 'at the office'

explanation.surface: Folk are seriously to blame for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At fault' reads as one phrase, but 'at' goes with the wordplay and 'fault, gravely so' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave wrongdoing that kills the soul's grace is the most serious category of transgression.

clue.text: Collaborating closely, but passing on nothing

parts.note: handing describes giving something on to another
love means zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Partners working tightly together yet sharing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties in close, often conspiratorial, partnership.

clue.text: Lodging for tramp

definitions.meaning: slang for a flat or place to live
to walk steadily on foot, to tramp

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: slang for a home, and a verb for trudging along.

clue.text: Principle is one a singer embraces

indicators.note: embraces means the singer's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A statement that a vocalist holds to a particular principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' in the clue is a link word, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation or underlying principle on which something rests is its groundwork.

clue.text: Seasoned jelly made of mussels, we hear

definitions.meaning: a dish of pork or meat set in its own spiced jelly
mussels said out loud matches muscles, and muscular strength is a synonym

explanation.surface: A recipe describing a spiced jelly made from shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works by sound: 'mussels' is heard as 'muscles', and muscle power means the same as the answer. 'Made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pressed meat terrine and physical strength or muscle.

clue.text: Type of verse I sent as composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet says the verse form they posted was written in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the poetry surface but signals rearranging I SENT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem of six six-line stanzas reusing the same end words is a set verse form.

clue.text: Lively agent covers both sides, but not to the same extent

indicators.note: covers means the agent's letters wrap around the sides

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the two sides are right and left; right is written in full
left is shortened to its abbreviation L

explanation.surface: A spy works for both parties, though not equally for each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But not to the same extent' says the two sides are given unequally: RIGHT in full, but L abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of energy and briskness is spry, a synonym.

clue.text: Take too long to inflict decisive defeat

definitions.meaning: a meeting that goes past its time limit does this
an army that swarms and crushes enemy positions does this

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to exceed a time limit and to overwhelm an enemy.

clue.text: Read out title and corresponding opening

indicators.note: out signals that the word Read is put out of its usual order

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: An instruction to announce someone's title and a matching start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal turning READ into DEAR; 'corresponding' means writing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter traditionally begins with this salutation, so it opens correspondence.

clue.text: Volunteers grabbing lifeboat to get otter

indicators.note: grabbing means the volunteers' letters seize and enclose the boat

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Noah's ark saved its passengers from the flood

explanation.surface: Reservists commandeer a rescue boat to catch an otter.
explanation.walkthrough: The otter is named after Henry Williamson's 1927 novel about a Devon otter.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known fictional example of the animal is the hero of Williamson's book.

clue.text: Resolution by one politician coming into effect soon

indicators.note: by means beside, so the resolution follows the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
an ending is the resolution of a story

explanation.surface: A motion from a lone MP is about to take effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' reads as a parliamentary motion, but it means the outcome of a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen is imminent or looming.

clue.text: Artistically presented Madam Butterfly

definitions.meaning: a heavily made-up woman, a madam whose face is coloured, or one rendered on canvas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Madam Butterfly' reads as Puccini's opera, but the clue splits there into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a rouged woman and a species of Vanessa butterfly.

clue.text: Hard to avoid sigh of relief, finding a seat

indicators.note: to avoid means the hard letter is dropped from the exclamation

parts.note: phew is what you say when relieved
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone escapes something difficult and, relieved, finds somewhere to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long bench in a church is a place to sit.

clue.text: Vital soldier dropped on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier is placed on top of the next piece, as a parachutist lands

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a mount is a hill, as in Mount Sinai

explanation.surface: A crucial paratrooper parachuted onto a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of supreme importance is essential, a synonym.

clue.text: Gesture, should I be unable to find material

parts.note: a sign is a gesture made to communicate
should I be unable means if I can't

explanation.surface: Someone signals that they might not find the cloth they need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like fabric, but it means important.
explanation.definitionFit: Something material to a case is important or relevant, like the answer.

clue.text: Having entire correspondence in dialect, needs translation

indicators.note: needs translation means these words must be converted, so their letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A letter written wholly in a local dialect has to be translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' suggests letters, but here it means matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match in every respect are exactly the same.

clue.text: Examine surroundings, wriggling toe in corner

indicators.note: wriggling means twisting about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone squirming their toe in a corner while surveying the area.
explanation.definitionFit: To scout an area before acting is to survey the terrain, a synonym.

clue.text: Manage to study almost all fish

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: almost all means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to troll is to fish by trailing a baited line

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fit in study and nearly all their fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is a verb here, trolling for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or direct something is to have command of it.

clue.text: Habitually row over thickness

definitions.meaning: a ferry that regularly travels a route over water does this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is the rowing kind, plying back and forth over water; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for regular travel by boat and a noun for a layer of material.

clue.text: Start to prepare criticism for show before first night

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a review is a critic's assessment

explanation.surface: A critic gets ready to write about a show before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance shown to an audience ahead of the official opening is a sneak showing.

clue.text: One wouldn't want to set off on a walk here

definitions.text: One wouldn't want to set off on a walk here

parts.words: One wouldn't want to set off on a walk here
parts.note: set off reads as begin a stroll, but means detonate: a place with buried explosives

explanation.definitionFit: An area sown with explosive charges is where stepping could trigger a blast.

clue.text: Hurry to accept top honours for type of pastry

indicators.note: to accept means the hurry word takes the honours inside it

parts.note: to fly is to rush
in bridge, the ace and king are the top honours, A and K

explanation.surface: Rushing to accept leading awards for a pastry contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link. The pastry is flaky pastry, which forms thin crisp layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry made in thin crisp layers is named for those layers.

clue.text: Taking offence

definitions.meaning: the act of stealing, taking what is not yours

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the act of stealing and also names that crime.

clue.text: His services are required with troublesome frequency

definitions.text: His services are required with troublesome frequency

parts.words: His services are required with troublesome frequency
parts.note: troublesome frequency seems to mean too often, but means a radio wavelength or musical pitch that is off

explanation.definitionFit: A technician who adjusts pianos or radios to the right pitch or wavelength.

clue.text: Title of the late king?

parts.note: late reads as dead, but means not ready; the nickname of Ethelred, an English king

explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred II, king of England around 1000, bore a nickname that actually meant ill-advised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone late is not prepared, and this was Ethelred's epithet.

clue.text: This vegetable needs a month to come up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: May is a month

explanation.surface: A vegetable takes a month to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy tropical tuber is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: One offers lots to throw caution to the winds?

indicators.note: throw means toss about, so these letters are scattered
to the winds means letters flung around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A seller recklessly puts everything up for grabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw caution to the winds' is an idiom for recklessness, but 'throw ... to the winds' signals mixing up CAUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale where items are put up in numbered batches for bidding.

clue.text: Order any article missing in set

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

indicators.note: missing means the article is taken out of the word any

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone ordering any item absent from a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a TV set, here the British slang word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A television receiver is called a set, and British slang shortens it.

clue.text: Bark and blossom

definitions.meaning: a barque, a sailing ship, such as the Pilgrims' 1620 vessel
a flower of spring, such as hawthorn blossom or trailing arbutus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' looks like a dog or tree, but it is a variant spelling of barque, the ship that carried the Pilgrims to America.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Pilgrim Fathers' ship and to hawthorn flowers.
